title: I've been building Deep Fried, a turn-based dungeon-diving roguelite with an emphasis on cooking meals out of monster parts!
author: rychder
selftext:
This is my first game that I've worked on and I'm looking for feedback on what can be improved.

The idea: you dive into a living dungeon called the Gullet, fight monsters, butcher them into ingredients, and cook meals at camp between floors. Meals are your only source of mana and health regen so the quality of the meals is essential. You can head home after any floor to bank your haul, but if you die , the dungeon takes half.

It's free and plays in your browser: [https://ryderlink.itch.io/deep-fried](https://ryderlink.itch.io/deep-fried)

I know dungeon divers are a dime-a-dozen, I'm not looking to be the next big thing in the genre. I just want to hear feedback from gamers on what I should be thinking about in future projects.

This was generated with the help of claude code and gemini for visual asset generation.

What I'd especially love feedback on:

\- \*\*The first 10 minutes.\*\* Was it clear what to do? Where did you get confused?

\- \*\*Cooking.\*\* Did it feel rewarding, or like the choice you made didn't have enough effect?

\- \*\*Difficulty.\*\* Did any enemies feel too OP?

\- \*\*Anything that felt clunky,\*\* broke, or made you want to quit.
